description: An oil painting of a grey-haired man in a black coat with a white clerical collar band, seated at a rough wooden table with an open ledger and a few coins, extending his open hand to an elderly man in a knit cap and worn brown coat who holds a coin; an older woman in a patterned headscarf and dark shawl clings to the old man's arm. The setting is a dim rustic timber-and-stone interior with a wall-mounted oil lamp and a wooden box. Dress, lamp and furnishings read as 18th or 19th century. No text, no frame; a small sparkle logo in the bottom-right corner. Nothing graphic.
reason: Shows a clergyman taking coins from a poor elderly couple in a 19th-century cottage, not the 1971 Smithsonian Agreement on currency realignment between nations. The oil lamp, dress and rustic interior are 18th or 19th century, a clear anachronism for a 1971 card.
